captionV1:
A PPM visit can be booked, the engineer can arrive on time, and the job can still stall because the part they need isn’t on the van.

That means another visit to arrange, more time spent chasing, and a maintenance issue left open for longer.

When planning a visit, ask the person reporting the issue to include the asset details, symptoms and any photos they can provide. Then have the office check that information against the job history and confirm likely parts before the engineer sets off.

We think good job information is what turns a planned visit into a prepared one. Where does the parts check sit in your PPM process?
